recognize_zh: 高倍下單一母細胞：核佔細胞大部分、染色質細緻均勻、核輪廓略凹，細胞質少呈淡藍並有一個小空泡；此張看不到明確的嗜天青顆粒或 Auer 小體，只能確認為母細胞，顆粒特徵需參考同系列其他圖。
features: Single blast about twice the diameter of a red cell
Very high N:C ratio with a slightly indented nuclear contour
Fine, evenly dispersed chromatin; nucleoli indistinct
Narrow rim of pale blue cytoplasm with a single small clear vacuole
No definite azurophilic granules or Auer rods visible in this image
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at high power shows a single blast with a very high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, a slightly indented nucleus with finely dispersed chromatin and indistinct nucleoli, and a narrow rim of pale blue cytoplasm containing a small vacuole. Definite azurophilic granules and Auer rods are not seen in this cell. The morphology is that of a blast but does not by itself demonstrate the granular feature of granular ALL. Findings are compatible with a lymphoblast in the context of granular ALL; lineage must be confirmed by MPO cytochemistry and flow cytometry.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts often have more visible nucleoli and may contain Auer rods; MPO positivity and myeloid antigens distinguish them.
Burkitt cells have deeply basophilic cytoplasm with multiple lipid vacuoles, rather than a single vacuole in pale cytoplasm.
Hematogones have more homogeneous, smudgy condensed chromatin and scant cytoplasm and are a benign maturing population by flow cytometry.
